testcase.name: a hop hovering around 25 m stays counted once entered, rather than flickering
the estimate decreases at every point of the return leg and is zero at the origin
a counted hop leaves the band only below 20 m, and a far hop only below 45 m
a straight track's path home is the sum of its legs, with no hop from a walker standing on the last point
the origin's last hop is included when the track has an origin waypoint, and is zero when the origin is the first point
a hop under 25 m is measured but omitted from the total
a hop between 25 and 50 m is added as-is and does not degrade
a track with no usable points has no path home, and a single point has a zero-length track with a measured hop
a hop over 50 m is added and marks the estimate degraded
parallel legs 15 m apart are not joined - 8 m apart they are
a doubled-back track is joined at the points the walker re-occupied and reads the ground still ahead
